lesson.l01.title: Question First!
lesson.l01.objective1: Recognize when a business question is underspecified
lesson.l01.objective2: Build a structured analytical brief: entity, timeframe, behavior, population, metric, decision
lesson.l01.objective3: State what a chosen definition does and doesn't capture
dialogue.l01_briefing.line1: We need to know - are customers becoming less loyal? Leadership wants an answer by Friday.
dialogue.l01_briefing.line2: Just tell me: loyal or not. Shouldn't take long, right?
dialogue.l01_briefing.line3: Before you touch any data - what does 'less loyal' actually mean here? That question could mean five different things.
dialogue.l01_briefing.line4: Let's build a proper analytical brief before we commit to an answer.
dialogue.l01_investigation.line1: Here's what NovaMart Go tracks: signups, purchases, app logins, subscription status - about a year of history.
dialogue.l01_investigation.line2: Notice something? 'Loyal' isn't a column in that data. We have to decide what it means before we can measure it.
dialogue.l01_investigation.line3: Let's build a brief: who we're counting, over what time, based on what behavior - and what decision it's actually for.
dialogue.l01_independent_intro.line1: Good. Now try one on your own - no hints this time.
dialogue.l01_independent_intro.line2: NovaMart Plus wants to know: is engagement dropping? Same drill - build the brief.
dialogue.l01_twist.line1: Before you send that off, let's check something. Same customers, same behavior - repeat purchases - measured two ways.
dialogue.l01_twist.line2: Only the time window changed. Look what happens to the story.
dialogue.l01_debrief.line1: Good instinct - you built a brief before answering, not after. That's the whole lesson.
dialogue.l01_debrief.line2: Whoever defines the question defines the answer. Time window, population, metric - every one of those is a choice, and every choice changes the story.
dialogue.l01_debrief.line3: Next time NovaMart asks you something 'simple,' the first move is still the same: what exactly are we measuring, and what decision does it serve?
lesson.l01.field.entity.prompt: Who or what are we actually measuring?
lesson.l01.field.entity.hint: The 'entity' is the unit you're counting. Get this wrong and every later number is about the wrong thing.
lesson.l01.field.time_horizon.hint: A short window catches recent shifts but is noisier. A long window is more stable but can hide recent change.
lesson.l01.field.behavior.hint: Different behaviors tell different stories - a login isn't the same commitment as a renewal.
lesson.l01.field.population.prompt: Which customers should even be included?
lesson.l01.field.population.hint: Including customers who couldn't possibly show the behavior yet - like brand-new signups - can quietly bias the result.
lesson.l01.option.population.active_last: Only customers active in the last year
lesson.l01.field.metric.prompt: How do we turn that into one number?
lesson.l01.field.metric.hint: The metric you pick determines what 'went up' or 'went down' even means.
lesson.l01.field.decision_support.prompt: What decision should this number actually inform?
lesson.l01.field.decision_support.hint: A brief that isn't tied to a real decision is just trivia - this is what keeps the analysis useful.
lesson.l01.option.decision_support.loyal: Whether to launch a loyalty program
lesson.l01.option.decision_support.escal: Whether to escalate this to leadership as urgent
lesson.l01.field.window_choice.prompt: Which time window should this analysis actually use?
lesson.l01.field.window_choice.hint: The PM wants to know if something is happening now. A window that's too long could hide a recent, real shift.
lesson.l01.field.limitation.prompt: What does this metric NOT tell you, even once you've picked a window?
lesson.l01.field.limitation.hint: A good analyst states what's still uncertain, not just the headline number.
